solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: South African lynx runs ahead of boor in grass

parts.note: R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the boor is placed inside the grass

parts.note: the oat plant is a cereal grass
an oik is a crude, loutish person

explanation.surface: A wild cat prowls through long grass, a lout running ahead of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' places R before the grass-and-boor combination, giving ROOIKAT. Oik is British slang for an uncouth person.
explanation.definitionFit: The rooikat, Afrikaans for red cat, is the South African name for the caracal, a wild feline with tufted ears.

clue.text: In sunshine, it's surprising infidels among the Ottomans

indicators.note: being in something means the exclamation sits inside the sunshine

explanation.surface: In the sun, unbelievers are surprisingly found among the Turks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayah was the Ottoman term for non-Muslim subjects of the Sultan, liable to tax, so unbelievers in Turkish eyes.

clue.text: Outsiders displace Gift Aid's regular contributions

definitions.note: a tool name plural in form, like pliers, for a singular instrument

indicators.note: regular contributions are payments made at even intervals, so every second letter of the phrase is kept

explanation.surface: Outsiders push aside regular donations made under Gift Aid, the British tax scheme for charity giving.
explanation.walkthrough: Outsiders looks like people; it is a burglar's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An oustiti is a pair of nippers for turning a key from the outer side of a lock, also called outsiders.

clue.text: Red-flowering plant starts in area in front of house, perhaps carnation coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top
the starts of words are their first letters, taken from each word of the phrase that follows

parts.note: opening letters of the five words
a carnation is one kind of pink, a Dianthus

explanation.surface: A gardener's tip: something red flowering in the bed before the house, maybe carnations sprouting.
explanation.walkthrough: AIFOH and PINK together are reversed in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Kniphofia is the genus of red-hot pokers, which bear spikes of red and orange flowers.

clue.text: Obstacles for cavalry: louts rode unsteadily on horseback

indicators.note: riding unsteadily means wobbling about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: a jockey who is up is mounted

explanation.surface: Yobs wobbling along on horses hit barriers meant for mounted troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Trous-de-loup, French for wolf-holes, are conical pits with a stake at the bottom, dug to stop attacking horsemen.

clue.text: Help with vessel, Sinbad's cutter?

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to help them

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand with a pot, while the sailor of the Arabian Nights brandishes a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship for Sinbad; it is only a jar. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A handjar is a Persian or Middle Eastern dagger, the sort of curved weapon a hero of the Arabian Nights might carry.

clue.text: Stop Her Highness seizing ring

indicators.note: to seize is to grab hold of, so the royal title wraps round the ring

explanation.surface: An order to halt a princess who is grabbing jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoh, a variant of ho, is an old cry or verb meaning halt or cease, so to stop.

clue.text: Aged female relative's sister capturing a brother's heart

indicators.note: to capture is to take in, so the sister holds the article

parts.note: a sister in a religious order

indicators.note: a heart is the centre, so only the central letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An old aunt's sister holds her brother dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aged' means archaic: the word is old, not the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Naunt is an obsolete form of aunt, from 'mine aunt' misdivided as 'my naunt'.

clue.text: Flowery muslin stuff seen on lion-tamer, more than half visible

indicators.note: only the larger part of the name shows, so its tail is dropped

parts.note: to jam is to stuff or cram
the biblical Daniel survived the lions' den

explanation.surface: Floral cloth spotted on a circus lion-tamer, partly showing.
explanation.walkthrough: Four letters of the six-letter DANIEL are kept. Lion-tamer looks like a circus act; it is the prophet in the lions' den.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamdani is a fine Bengali muslin woven with floral designs, so a patterned cotton fabric.

clue.text: Upset once scriptural teaching is on new division in Biblical chapter

parts.note: chapters of the Bible are split into verses

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled that Sunday school is moving on to a fresh section of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for religious education, a British school subject. In a down clue, on means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Renverse is an obsolete verb meaning to overturn or reverse, from French renverser, so 'once' marks it archaic.

clue.text: Stick Old Testament in non-standard agreement for faith schools

indicators.note: being placed in something means the stick and the testament go inside the agreement

parts.note: a slangy, non-standard form of yes
a shiv is slang for a knife; to stick is to stab

explanation.surface: An instruction about wedging scripture into an informal deal for religious schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like glue or a twig; it is a verb, to stab, as with a prison knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeshiva is an Orthodox Jewish college for Talmudic study; yeshivoth is its Hebrew plural, so religious schools.

clue.text: What might make trunk sticky, foul-minded nurses?

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the phrase holds the letters wanted within it

parts.note: the letters straddle the hyphenated phrase

explanation.surface: A smutty thinker caring for something that gums up a tree trunk, or perhaps an elephant's.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside fOUL-MINded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulmin is a brown gummy substance exuded by elm and other trees, so it can make bark sticky.

clue.text: Unfinished poem, hard in Armenian

indicators.note: not finished means the word stops short and loses its last letter

parts.note: H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A half-written verse, a tough one, in the Armenian language.
explanation.walkthrough: HAIKU loses its U, then H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Haikh is the Armenians' own name for themselves, after their legendary ancestor Hayk, so an Armenian person.

clue.text: Small worry with double nucleus shaped like an arrowhead

indicators.note: the nucleus is a word's central letter, and doubling it means writing that letter twice

parts.note: S for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A minor fret with a twin core, like an arrow's point.
explanation.walkthrough: AGITATE has seven letters and its fourth, T, is the nucleus; doubling it gives AGITTATE after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagittate, from Latin sagitta for arrow, describes leaves and other botanical parts with a pointed, barbed triangular outline.

clue.text: Perth beggar's lifted pouch, form of lure that is found around New Zealand

indicators.note: lifted means raised, so in this down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: a pouch is a small bag

indicators.note: found around means placed on both sides, so the reworked letters enclose the country
a form of something is a reshaping, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish vagrant has stolen a purse, tempting enough to be found around the Antipodes.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth is the Scottish city, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaberlunzie was a licensed Scottish beggar or wandering mendicant, a word made famous by Scott.

clue.text: Tropical plants perish following repeated initiation for Banks in choppy China Sea

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, written twice as in page references

indicators.note: being in something means that letter is placed among the sea's letters
choppy water is broken and churned, so these letters are tossed into a new order
an initiation is a beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Plants dying off after Joseph Banks, the botanist, twice set sail across a rough Asian sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks suggests the plant-collecting botanist Sir Joseph Banks, but only lends a B. ff is the familiar short form for 'and following pages'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieffenbachia, the dumb cane, is a genus of tropical American foliage plants widely grown as houseplants.

clue.text: Headed mushroom consumed by Henry?

parts.note: the cep is the porcini mushroom
Hal is the familiar name for Henry, as in Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Was the mushroom gobbled by a man called Henry?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as Henry having consumed it: Henry's name comes before what he ate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cephalate, from Greek kephalē, describes an animal having a distinct head, so it is headed.

clue.text: See someone gathering stuff on ground that covers Channel Islands up?

definitions.text: See someone gathering stuff on ground that covers Channel Islands up?

parts.note: v. stands for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: to cover is to sit over and around, so the gatherer's letters wrap the islands

parts.note: one who rakes leaves from a lawn

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Look out for someone collecting stuff from the shore, the thing that blankets the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: vraic is seaweed gathered on Channel Islands beaches for fertiliser.
explanation.definitionFit: A vraicker is a Guernsey or Jersey gatherer of vraic, the seaweed collected from shores as manure.

clue.text: Sordid artist's right hand, unknown aide, understood about strike hours

indicators.note: going about something means wrapping around it, so the word for understood surrounds the strike and the hours

parts.note: radio-speak for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A seedy painter's helper and mystery assistant, receiving word about strike hours, as in a labour dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action but simply means hit. Roger is the radio reply meaning message understood.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyparographer, from Greek rhyparos meaning filthy, is a painter of mean, squalid or vulgar subjects.

clue.text: About time to neuter mounting dog

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in this down entry the string reads upwards

parts.note: to spay is to sterilise a female animal

explanation.surface: It is about time the randy dog was neutered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' plays on canine behaviour; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A yapster is an old word for a small yapping dog, a cur.

clue.text: Cut off old-style pledge, upset (at giving way to crude signature?)

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this down entry the word reads upwards
giving way means stepping aside so that something else takes the place

parts.note: in an older sense, to dedicate was to devote or pledge solemnly
a cross made by someone who cannot write

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned vow is overturned when a rough scrawl replaces something.
explanation.walkthrough: In DEDICATE the AT becomes X, giving DEDICXE, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To excide is to excise or remove by cutting, so excided means cut away.

clue.text: In Rhineland I must interrupt visit for "rock" in body of water

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the German pronoun goes inside the verb

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A German traveller breaks off a visit to the Lorelei, the famous rock on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' is in quotation marks because it means rocking, not a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A seiche is a standing wave that makes a lake or enclosed bay slosh back and forth, a rocking of the water.

clue.text: Spontaneous terror spree before middle of autumn

parts.note: a little terror is a mischievous child, an imp
a romp is a lively frolic

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, here the central pair of a six-letter word

parts.note: the central two letters of autumn

explanation.surface: A wild burst of fear and fun in the middle of the autumn season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terror' suggests fear, but a little terror is a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: Impromptu means done without preparation or rehearsal, on the spur of the moment, which is spontaneous.

clue.text: Brass work that's tedious moving over to first place

indicators.note: moving a thing means taking it from where it is and setting it down at the front

explanation.surface: Polishing the brass is a boring job.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass looks like the metal; it is slang for money. The O of CHORE moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is old slang for money, from gold coins' yellow colour, as brass is also slang for cash.

clue.text: Leg joint no longer used without difficulties when cycling?

indicators.note: cycling round means letters taken from the front are carried round to the back

parts.note: a clean run is one free of problems

explanation.surface: A knee or ankle that troubles a rider on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first two letters of CLEAN, CL, to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancle is an obsolete spelling of ankle, the hinge between the foot and the lower leg.

clue.text: Tough paper in House of Commons that initially British country rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the whole string is written from right to left
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

explanation.surface: A tough Westminster document turned down by the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: HC, T and UK together are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Kutch is a packet of strong vellum or parchment-like sheets between which goldbeaters hammer gold leaf.

clue.text: Related to lyricists accepting English and Australian backing of Stones (from The Animals)

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the adjective for lyricists holds the rest
backing means running in reverse, so the Australian abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: Songwriters taking on English and Australian support for the Rolling Stones and The Animals, two British rock bands.
explanation.walkthrough: Stones and The Animals look like 1960s bands; the definition is literal: stones that come from animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A bezoar is a hard concretion formed in the stomach of goats and other beasts, once prized as an antidote; bezoardic is its adjective.

clue.text: Wader leaving northernmost island again

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the bird's name

parts.note: I for island, the top one in this down entry

explanation.surface: A wading bird flies away from a far-northern isle once more.
explanation.walkthrough: IBIS has two Is; northernmost picks the one at the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bis, Latin for twice, is called out as an encore and marks a passage to be repeated.

clue.text: Sydney's conmen run crooked resort

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of true, so the next word's letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Australian swindlers running a dodgy holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney's signals Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a rort is a scam or fiddle, so rorters are people who work dishonest schemes.

clue.text: Frenchwoman's distracted European Parliament with the Queen expected

explanation.surface: A French woman is flustered as Brussels politicians await a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a French adjective in its feminine form, hence Frenchwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Éperdue is the feminine of French éperdu, meaning frantic or beside oneself, used in English for someone overwhelmed.
